Add an inclusion criterion to a criteria pipeline

Source: R/criteria.R
include.Rd

Add an inclusion criterion to a criteria pipeline

Usage

include(criteria, predicate, label, category = NULL, reason = NULL)

Arguments

criteria

A cf_criteria object (or NULL to start a new one).

predicate

A one-sided formula or a function evaluated row-wise.

label

A short human-readable description of this criterion. See the Labels section.

category

An optional string grouping this step with others for display (e.g. "Valid age"). NULL leaves it uncategorised.

reason

An optional short description of the rows this step removes, shown in diagram exclusion boxes. NULL (default) uses label for exclusion steps; for inclusion steps it should be set. See the Labels section.

Value

The updated cf_criteria object.

Missing values

A predicate that evaluates to NA for a row is treated differently by the two step types, and the difference changes denominators:

  • include() treats NA as failing: the row is removed. Write include(~ age >= 18) and rows with missing age are excluded here.

  • exclude() treats NA as not matching: the row is kept. Write exclude(~ withdrew) and rows with missing withdrew stay in.

To make the intent explicit, handle NA in the predicate itself, e.g. include(~ !is.na(age) & age >= 18) or exclude(~ is.na(withdrew) | withdrew). Grouped steps (group_include(), group_exclude(), select_within()) always remove rows whose by value is NA. To see the raw predicate values, NA included, use criteria_status() with mode = "independent".

Labels

A step has up to two pieces of text, and diagrams put each next to the count it describes:

  • label names the step. For include(), group_include() and select_within() it describes the rows kept ("Aged 18 or over"), and an uncategorised step's main box in as_consort_diagram() shows it with the number remaining. For exclude() and group_exclude() it describes the rows removed ("Withdrew consent"), so the diagram shows it in the exclusion box with the number removed, and the main box below reads "Remaining (n = ...)".

  • reason describes the rows removed, for exclusion boxes. Exclusion steps default to their label. For inclusion steps the label would read backwards in an exclusion box ("Aged 18 or over (n=6)" for six people under 18), so give a reason ("Under 18"). Without one, an uncategorised inclusion step's exclusion box just says "Excluded", and one listed under a category falls back to its label with a warning.

Attrition tables list every step by label, beside a "Removed" column.

See also

Other criteria builders: cf_criteria(), cf_criterion(), check_criteria(), exclude(), group_exclude(), group_include(), randomise(), select_within()

Examples

cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Adults", category = "Valid age",
          reason = "Under 18")
#> Cohort criteria pipeline  (1 step)
#>    1. [+][~] (include) {Valid age} Adults
#>           age >= 18
#>           removes: Under 18
